study type: Subgroup analysis of a cohort study
cohort: 7,029 Saudi mothers from a Riyadh mother and baby cohort study
finding: Prepregnancy obesity in Saudi women is highly prevalent and associated with increased odds of gestational diabetes, hypertensive events in pregnancy, labor induction, failed induction of labor, cesarean section delivery, and macrosomia, while underweight women had increased odds of delivering low birth weight infants.
mod_finding: Obese women had increased odds of induction of labour, failed IOL, and delivery by emergency caesarean section, while overweight women had increased odds of CS delivery and failed IOL.
